acceptance.claim: The daily job selects the same kind of notices with date_of_suspension equal to the report date (today only) and builds the Excel file 'OCMS_RIP_Hirer_Driver_Report_<date>.xlsx' with a summary sheet and a data sheet. A missed run loses that day, because no other date range is queried.
acceptance.quote: AND CAST(sn.date_of_suspension AS DATE) = CAST(:suspensionDate AS DATE)
acceptance.missing: Selection by one date, file name and the two sheets are proved. Contradicting / not proved: 'today only' is true only until the first run. RipHirerDriverReportJob is a singleton Spring @Component whose field 'reportDate' is only set when null or empty (initialize(), JOB line 268-272); no line resets it to null and cleanup() does nothing. Read in code (not run): after the first execution in a JVM, later scheduled runs reuse that first date until the service restarts or a manual run sets another date. [Medium confidence: from reading the code; runtime not tested; needs verification in UAT with two consecutive days.] Also the claim 'no other date range is queried' is right for the scheduled run, but DailyReportController (line 97) allows a manual run for a given date.
acceptance.fix_en: The daily job selects un-revived PS-RP2 notices where the current offender is a deceased hirer or driver and date_of_suspension equals the report date, and builds 'OCMS_RIP_Hirer_Driver_Report_<date>.xlsx' with a Summary sheet and a data sheet. The report date is set to today when the job instance has no date yet (the field is not reset after a run, so repeated scheduled runs in the same running instance may reuse the first date - needs verification). A manual run for a chosen date exists in DailyReportController.
